rules.title: Query on IQueryable, materialise last
rules.what: Filter, project and paginate on the IQueryable; call ToList()/AsEnumerable() only after, never before the filters.
rules.why: Materialising first pulls the whole table into application memory and filters there: transfer, memory and CPU for rows nobody needs.
rules.how: Where/Select/Take before ToListAsync(); keyset pagination (Where(x => x.Id > lastId).Take(n)).

patterns.note: Filter applied after materialisation: the query ran without it.

verify.how: Generated SQL (ToQueryString or logging) contains the WHERE and the limit.

rules.title: Read-only queries untracked and projected
rules.what: Read-only queries use AsNoTracking() and a Select projection to a DTO rather than tracked entities with cascading Include.
rules.why: Change tracking snapshots every entity for nothing on a read; cascading Include loads whole graphs for a few fields.
rules.how: query.AsNoTracking().Select(x => new Dto { ... }); split queries for large Include graphs.

patterns.note: Chained Include; check whether a projection would do.

verify.how: Read paths use AsNoTracking or projections.

rules.title: Any() for existence
rules.what: Use Any() for existence tests, not Count() compared to zero; enumerate an IEnumerable once.
rules.why: Count() walks every element when an existence test stops at the first.
rules.how: if (items.Any()) ...; materialise once with ToList() when the sequence is reused.

patterns.note: Count() used as an existence test.

rules.title: async all the way
rules.what: Never block on a task with .Result, .Wait() or GetAwaiter().GetResult() in request code; await end to end.
rules.why: A blocking wait pins a thread-pool thread: more threads, more memory, and deadlock risk under load.
rules.how: Make the caller async and await; ConfigureAwait(false) in libraries.

rules.title: IHttpClientFactory, not new HttpClient
rules.what: Obtain HTTP clients from IHttpClientFactory (or one static instance); never new HttpClient() per call.
rules.why: One client per call exhausts sockets and repeats the TLS handshake on every request.
rules.how: services.AddHttpClient<T>(); typed clients with timeouts; response compression and caching headers on the server side.

patterns.note: HttpClient constructed; fine once at start-up, a defect per request.

verify.how: No HttpClient constructed in request code.

rules.title: Background services driven by events
rules.what: A BackgroundService reacts to messages or signals rather than polling a state in a tight loop.
rules.why: A loop with a short Task.Delay queries the database or an API continuously to catch a rare change.
rules.how: Consume a queue (Channel<T>, a broker), use PeriodicTimer with a justified interval when polling is unavoidable.

patterns.note: Polling loop with a short delay (under 10 s).

verify.how: Polling interval justified and documented, or replaced by an event source.

rules.title: Bounded caches, cheap strings and logs
rules.what: Use IMemoryCache with SizeLimit/expiration instead of a static Dictionary; StringBuilder for repeated concatenation; structured log templates instead of interpolated messages.
rules.why: A static dictionary grows until restart; += on strings allocates per iteration; an interpolated log message is built even when the level is off.
rules.how: IMemoryCache with AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow and Size; StringBuilder; _logger.LogDebug("x={X}", x).

patterns.note: Static dictionary; check it is bounded if used as a cache.
Interpolated log message; a template defers formatting.

verify.how: Caches bounded; no string += in loops; log calls use templates.
